description: sort_tasks(tasks) should sort items by priority (high > medium > low) then deadline ascending, but inverted priority values cause low priority to be sorted first.

tests.test_taskmgr.py:
from taskmgr import sort_tasks

def test_empty():
    # Passes before fix
    assert sort_tasks([]) == []

def test_same_priority_deadline_order():
    # Passes before fix (same priority)
    t = [
        {'id': 1, 'priority': 'high', 'deadline': 5},
        {'id': 2, 'priority': 'high', 'deadline': 2},
    ]
    res = sort_tasks(t)
    assert [x['id'] for x in res] == [2, 1]

def test_multi_priority():
    t = [
        {'id': 1, 'priority': 'low', 'deadline': 1},
        {'id': 2, 'priority': 'high', 'deadline': 10},
        {'id': 3, 'priority': 'medium', 'deadline': 5},
    ]
    res = sort_tasks(t)
    # high should come first, then medium, then low
    assert [x['id'] for x in res] == [2, 3, 1]

def test_tie_breaking():
    t = [
        {'id': 1, 'priority': 'medium', 'deadline': 8},
        {'id': 2, 'priority': 'high', 'deadline': 3},
        {'id': 3, 'priority': 'high', 'deadline': 1},
    ]
    res = sort_tasks(t)
    assert [x['id'] for x in res] == [3, 2, 1]
